reason: Rilla's mobile posting does contain a near-perfect pain line ("As the first fully dedicated mobile engineer, you will clear today's velocity bottlenecks and take full ownership of our mobile codebase, crafting a lightning-fast, real-time experience for field users"), but the company fails every other screen: Sacra puts it at ~$70M ARR in April 2026 (+113% YoY, up from $51M) and profitable with ~100-150 employees and $78.9M raised from GV/Bessemer/Crew — roughly 5x above Bill's own declared ICP ceiling of $3M-$15M ARR; there is no leadership seat to sell into, since three technical co-founders already hold it (CTO Chris Martin, Head of Engineering Lukasz Niepolski, Chief AI Officer Michael Castellanos); and the situation is inverted — Bill fixes stalled delivery on legacy mobile-and-desktop codebases running a pre-AI SDLC, whereas Rilla is a 2019-founded AI-native company whose stated culture is shipping "at lightning speed," so its mobile bottleneck is youthful under-investment (never had a dedicated mobile engineer) rather than a legacy transformation, and they are explicitly solving it by hiring one senior engineer in-office in NYC at $230K-$375K, not by renting a fractional exec in Utah. Vertical is also only adjacent: Rilla sells sales-coaching AI into the trades, it is not property-trades vertical SaaS like Xactimate or JobNimbus. The one matched job in the pack was a Director of Enterprise Sales, which confesses nothing about engineering delivery.
